paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: you can't earn God's blessing, and you can't finish what He started by working harder. Paul asks the Galatians whether they received the Spirit "by works of the law, or by hearing with faith" (Galatians 3:2). They began in the Spirit, and Paul asks if they are now "finishing in the flesh" (Galatians 3:3). I know that trap. I once tried to fix my own blurry edges with extra flour, and friend, the flour did NOT care.

Why does it matter? Because the law asks for everything. Paul quotes Scripture that says, "Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law" (Galatians 3:10). And the law "is not based on faith," it runs on doing (Galatians 3:12). But the same passage says, "The righteous will live by faith" (Galatians 3:11). Abraham is the example, because he "believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness" (Galatians 3:6).

Here is the good news, baker. "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us" (Galatians 3:13). He did that so the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles, and so "by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit" (Galatians 3:14). So you can rest your whole weight on Jesus, not on your own batch record. Keep believing, keep hearing, and keep the ovens ready.
